title: Jacob, father of R' Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: According to the testimony of his son Rav Nachman, his father was among the scribes of Mar Shmuel’s judges, as explained in [Bava Metzia 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.16b.9).

He was indeed a great man, as we find in [Beitzah 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.26b.2): Rabbah bar Rav Huna expounded, and Rav Nachman said to him, “My father taught it.” Hyman likewise cites Zevachim 53a: a tanna recited these before Rav Nachman, who said to him, “Thus my father told me.” We have already explained in the entry on Rav Nachman that an unqualified “Rav Nachman” is bar Jacob, even according to Rashi’s view.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson text of Bava Metzia 16b:9 names Rav Nachman and calls his father one of the scribes, or clerks, of Mar Shmuel’s judges. It does not name the father; the identification with Jacob is Hyman’s.

Hyman cites Beitzah 26a; the matching account is at 26b:2 in the linked edition and names Rabbah bar Rav Huna. Rashi there explains אבא תני as “he is speaking about his father,” hence “My father taught it.” The Zevachim exchange was not found in the consulted text of 52b–53b; its locator and wording are reported here on Hyman’s authority. A tanna in this exchange is a reciter of a teaching. The concluding cross-reference and identification of unqualified Rav Nachman with bar Jacob are Hyman’s.
